sections.h2: What can a bookkeeper help with?
sections.html:
• Recording sales, purchases and expenses
  • Bank and credit-card reconciliation
  • Invoicing and chasing payments
  • Payroll processing
  • Preparing VAT or sales tax returns
  • Setting up cloud accounting software

sections.h2: When should you hire a bookkeeper?
sections.html:
• You are behind on your books or dreading tax season
  • You spend evenings and weekends on admin
  • You want monthly figures to manage cash flow
  • You are moving to cloud accounting software

sections.h2: Questions to ask before you hire
sections.html:
When you compare quotes, these questions help you find the right fit:

  1. Which accounting software are you experienced with?
  2. Do you work remotely or on-site?
  3. Are you certified by or a member of a professional body (such as AIPB in the US, or ICB or AAT in the UK)?
  4. How do you charge — hourly, monthly or per transaction?

Every business and project is different, so prices vary. The main factors are:

  • Volume of transactions each month
  • Frequency (weekly, monthly, quarterly)
  • Additional services such as payroll or VAT
  • Whether there is a backlog to catch up on

The simplest way to understand the cost for your situation is to compare a few quotes side by side.

faqs.q: How often should a bookkeeper update my books?
faqs.a: Most small businesses benefit from monthly bookkeeping. Busier businesses may prefer weekly updates.
Yes. With cloud accounting software, many bookkeepers work entirely remotely, giving you a wider choice of professionals.

faqs.q: Can a bookkeeper file my tax return?
faqs.a: Some can, but year-end accounts and tax returns are usually prepared by an accountant. Your bookkeeper’s records make that job faster and cheaper.
